Jaya here. When we finished the launch plan for our new leave-request page, everyone on the team felt good about it. So we did something a little uncomfortable: we asked Lalremsiami from the finance department to read it. I sent her the plan with a short note, asking her to mark anything that looked odd.
Two days later she came back with one line circled. Our plan said, "Staff will see the launch email on Monday morning." She asked, "What about people on the night shift or the plant floor, who don't open email at a desk?"
None of us had thought of it. We had all assumed everyone reads email at a desk. We added notices at the gate and a short talk at shift change.

Product head's note on the Q3 launch plan

Deepika's team has worked on the launch plan for a month. Last week she did something I'd like other teams to copy. She asked Usha, from our customer support department, to read the whole plan and tell her what looked odd. Nobody on the product team had talked to support. Usha came back in two days. She pointed out that the whole plan assumed customers would update the app themselves. "In support, we see most users don't update for months," she said. The team had never questioned it; it seemed obvious to all of them. Deepika has added an update reminder and a support script. I've suggested an outside reader for every future launch plan.

qa.a: Usha likely felt valued, as support's knowledge of real users was finally being used.

Thursday

Big lesson today. Our team has been polishing the launch plan for the new savings feature for weeks. Everyone agreed on everything, which I now think was the problem. On Monday I asked Kalyani from the legal team to read it. I felt a bit silly, sending it to someone outside. Today she came to my desk with one page marked in pencil. "You've all assumed users can sign up on the first day," she said. "But the approval for the new terms only comes through in the second week." Nobody on our team had thought to check. We'd all just believed it. We're moving the launch by one week. I felt embarrassed, then very grateful. Parul, next time ask an outsider sooner.
